name: Ironclad Agrisystems VertiRoot VX-22 Closed-Loop Hydroponic Column
product_name: Ironclad Agrisystems VertiRoot VX-22 Closed-Loop Hydroponic Column
description:
The VertiRoot VX-22 is a self-contained modular agricultural column measuring 4.2 meters tall and 0.9 meters in diameter, designed for dense urban installation in corridors, rooftops, abandoned infrastructure shafts, and repurposed parking structures throughout Meridian 88. Each column houses sixteen stacked growth rings fed by a recirculating nutrient solution managed by an onboard Cinderblock AI microcontroller that adjusts pH, dissolved oxygen, light spectrum from embedded LED arrays, and harvest timing autonomously. A single VX-22 column produces approximately 180 kilograms of leafy greens, legumes, or tuber crops annually using 94% less water than conventional agriculture through closed-loop condensate recovery.

The VX-22's defining innovation is its mycelial integration layer — a secondary biological network of edible fungi inoculated into the column's growth medium that processes root waste, suppresses pathogen blooms, and produces a secondary mushroom harvest from the same footprint without additional inputs. Ironclad licenses proprietary fungal strains that are genetically tagged, meaning any unauthorized propagation of the mycelium outside the licensed column triggers a legal claim under Meridian 88's Biological Asset Protection statutes. The columns connect to Ironclad's AgriNet data service via Saltmarsh Telecom uplinks, allowing remote diagnostics and automated nutrient cartridge delivery — also sold exclusively through Ironclad's supply chain.

Vertical column farms built from VX-22 arrays have become the primary food production infrastructure for Tier 2 and Tier 3 residential zones, as surface agriculture within Meridian 88's footprint collapsed following the Lake Erie algal iron events of the 2070s. Corporate cafeterias at Tier 1 facilities use premium VX-22 Pro configurations. In the lower districts, community co-ops pool resources to maintain shared column clusters, though dependency on Ironclad's proprietary nutrient cartridges and licensed strains creates a structural vulnerability that corporate enforcers and supply-chain leverage disputes have exploited more than once.
enables: mycelium-based waste processing at residential scale
biological asset tracking and enforcement systems
social_impact: The VertiRoot VX-22 has effectively made Ironclad Agrisystems the gatekeeper of caloric access for roughly 40% of Meridian 88's non-Tier-1 population. Community groups that built their food security around VX-22 arrays find themselves locked into Ironclad's supply ecosystem — nutrient cartridge price hikes in 2185 caused documented malnutrition spikes in three lower-district zones before community pressure forced a temporary rollback. The mycelial tagging system has been used in at least eleven prosecuted cases where residents attempted to cultivate independently propagated strains, with sentences ranging from fines to labor indenture contracts.
story_hooks: A community co-op discovers their VX-22 columns have been producing an unregistered fungal species for six months — one with unusual biochemical properties that Ironclad's AgriNet should have flagged immediately but did not

Someone is systematically contaminating Ironclad nutrient cartridge shipments to specific lower-district zones — the contamination is subtle, causing slow crop yield decline rather than obvious failure

A black-market botanist claims to have developed an open-source nutrient formula that breaks Ironclad's cartridge dependency, but distributing it puts her in violation of the Biological Asset Protection statutes
An Ironclad AgriNet data breach exposes the precise nutritional intake patterns of thousands of residents — the data is already being auctioned to Lazarus Pharmaceuticals and insurance actuaries
